explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD even hands them the words: “Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’” It's like a friend texting you exactly what to say before a tough conversation. Then comes the promise, “Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.”

I get it, friend. At a crossroads, my first question is usually how fast I can get out of there. But the LORD's question is “Where is the good way?” He's asking about the ancient paths, and the question is about the good way, not the quick one.

That sounds lovely, but it isn't the question in this verse. The LORD says to “Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’” The question is about finding the way. Then they are to walk in it, and the rest for their souls comes with that.

It would be nice if this one went the other way, wouldn't it? But the verse says, “But they said, ‘We will not walk in it!’” The LORD points to the good way and they turn it down. So the answer is False.

Right, baker. The text says, “But they said, ‘We will not walk in it!’” That's like your GPS saying turn left and you answering out loud, “I will not.” The LORD shows them the good way, and they refuse it.

Yes, friend. The LORD says, “I appointed watchmen over you and said, ‘Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.’” Their answer: “We will not listen!” That's a smoke alarm going off and somebody hollering at it to hush. The warning sounds, and they turn away from it.

That would've been a happy ending, friend. But the verse says, “But they answered, ‘We will not listen!’” Nobody promises anything here. The LORD appoints the watchmen and gives the warning, and the people say no.
Nice try, baker. In this verse the LORD is the One who appointed the watchmen. The people don't ask for any more. They answer, “We will not listen!”

explanations.answer: The nations and the whole earth
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “Therefore hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations, what will happen to them.” Then He adds, “Hear, O earth!” He isn't whispering this one. He's calling for everybody to listen in.

No priests are named in these verses, friend. The call goes out wider: “Hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations.” Then it goes wider still: “Hear, O earth!” That's a whole lot more people than one group.

The watchmen show up in the verse before this, friend. There the LORD says He appointed them over the people. But the call here goes to “O nations” and “O congregations.” After that He says, “Hear, O earth!”

You got it, baker. The LORD says the disaster comes “because they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction.” He also calls it “the fruit of their own schemes.” That's the reason He gives, and I'll stick with it.

Interesting, friend, because the very next verse talks about their burnt offerings and sacrifices. So this verse doesn't say the offerings stopped. The reason the LORD gives is that “they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction.”

explanations.answer: They bowed down to other gods
explanations.explanation: That isn't the reason given in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “because they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction.” I'm sticking to what He says here. Paying no attention to His word is the reason.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.” Those are plain words, and I won't dress them up. Offerings are on the altar, and He is not pleased with them.
I wish I could soften this one, friend, but the verse is plain. The LORD says, “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.” So the answer is True.

That's right, friend, and it's a heavy line. The LORD says, “fathers and sons alike will be staggered; friends and neighbors will perish.” I think this part is hard to read. It's a serious word, so I'll just let it stand.
I wish it said that, friend. But the verse says the opposite: “friends and neighbors will perish.” Fathers and sons are staggered, and friends and neighbors perish. It's a hard verse.

That's not what this verse says, friend. It says, “fathers and sons alike will be staggered; friends and neighbors will perish.” Captivity doesn't come up in it. The word for friends and neighbors is perish.

That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless.” Then He adds that “Their voice roars like the sea.” It's a heavy picture, and I'll just let the words stand.
That fits an army, friend, but it isn't what the verse says. The LORD says, “they are cruel and merciless.” Proud and boastful isn't in there. What is in there is that their voice roars like the sea.
The verse doesn't say that, friend. It says they “grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless.” Nothing is said about them being hungry. The LORD uses the words cruel and merciless.

You'd expect that, wouldn't you, friend? But the cry says, “We have heard the report; our hands hang limp.” Hands hanging limp aren't ready to grab anything. It goes on, “Anguish has gripped us.” So the answer is False.
That's right, baker. The cry is, “We have heard the report; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us.” Nobody is lacing up their boots here. They hear the news and their hands drop.

Yes, friend. The warning says, “Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road.” The reason is right there with it: “For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.” When the roads aren't safe, it's no day for errands.

It really is in there, baker. The verse says, “Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road.” Then it gives the reason: “For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.” So the answer is True.

That's it, baker. The verse says to mourn “for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.” The mourning is compared to what you'd do “for an only son.” It's a heavy picture, and I'd be careful not to rush past it.

No king is mentioned in this verse, friend. The reason given is, “for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.” The mourning is compared to grief for an only son. It's the destroyer coming that they're mourning.

Fields do come up in the verse before this, friend. But there it's a warning not to go out to them, because “the enemy has a sword.” The reason for mourning here is, “for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.”
That's right, baker. The LORD says, “All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers.” He goes on, “They are bronze and iron; all of them are corrupt.” Hardened is a strong word, and it's His.
Servants sounds a lot kinder, friend. But the verse says, “All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers.” The word is rebels. It's a hard one to hear.

Close in sound to the others, friend, but not what the verse says. The LORD says, “All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers.” They're called His people just before that. So rebels is the word.

I wish it worked, friend. But the verse says, “The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged.” The bellows blow fiercely and the fire is going. Still, the wicked are not purged, so the answer is False.

That's right, baker. The verse says, “The bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead with fire.” Then it adds, “The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged.” All that fire, and the wicked aren't purged.

That's the word, baker, and it's a heavy one. The verse says, “They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.” I think this one is hard to read, so I'll just let it sit for a moment.

That's a good guess, friend, but gold isn't in this furnace picture. The verse says, “They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.” The picture before that uses lead, bronze and iron. At the end, the word is silver.
Clay isn't in this picture, friend. The furnace has ore, lead, bronze, iron and silver. The last verse says, “They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.”
